previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius emphasizes that he seeks neither to grow beyond his proper station nor to usurp authority. He publicly conducts his affairs according to Roman law and the virtues expected of a respectable Roman landholder and commander. He declares the road and lake port officially open for commerce and hosts an opening festival intended to draw merchants, laborers, neighboring people and others whose ears may have reached the estate's name.

continuity.campaign_development: Valerius has formally opened the road from his main estate to the lake trade port and forward base for commerce. An opening festival brought merchants and local people to the station, increasing the port's visibility. Valerius has publicly emphasized adherence to Roman law, civic virtue and the limits of private authority, explicitly rejecting any claim to usurp public power. The road watchtowers and separate port defenses remain in place while the commercial face of the estate becomes more prominent.
